title: “I SEE HEAVEN OPEN.”
paragraphs: “I SEE HEAVEN OPEN.”
The rocks were already in their hands.
Stephen knew what was coming.
You don’t shout something like that to an angry mob unless you’ve already decided your life belongs to Someone else.

The accusations were flying.
Blasphemy.
Lies.
Distortion.
But Stephen didn’t defend himself the way most of us would.
He told the story.

From Abraham…
To Joseph…
To Moses…
To the prophets.
And then he drove the knife of truth straight into their hearts:
“You stiff-necked people… you always resist the Holy Spirit.” (Acts 7)
The room exploded.

Faces twisted.
Teeth grinding.
Fists tightening around stones.
But Stephen wasn’t looking at them anymore.
His eyes were fixed somewhere else.
And suddenly he cried out:
“I see heaven open and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God!”
Standing.
Not sitting.
As if Jesus Himself had risen to welcome a faithful witness home.
That was the final spark.
They dragged him outside the city.
No trial.
No mercy.
Just stones.

Crashing against bone.
Blood in the dust.
The roar of hatred drowning out everything else.
But listen to Stephen’s last words.
Not curses.
Not revenge.
“Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.”
And then—
“Lord, do not hold this sin against them.”
The first Christian martyr died sounding exactly like Jesus.
Forgiving the people killing him.
And standing there, watching it all?
A young man named Saul.
The same Saul who would later become Paul—the apostle who carried the Gospel across the world.

One faithful witness.
One fearless voice.
One man who refused to back down.
And heaven opened.
Here’s the truth we don’t say often enough:
Bold faith will cost you something.

Sometimes reputation.
Sometimes relationships.
Sometimes everything.
But Stephen saw what the world could not see.

Jesus is alive.
Jesus is reigning.
And Jesus is worth everything.
The same Savior who stood to receive Stephen now stands ready to receive anyone who turns to Him.

No matter your past.
No matter your failures.

The cross paid for it.
The empty tomb proved it.

Repent.
Believe.
Come home to Christ.
Because when you belong to Jesus—
Even death becomes a doorway into glory.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
